confirmed: Source identity is correct: IdeaBlocks: Expressing and Reusing Divergent Intents for Graphic Design Exploration using Generative AI, by DaEun Choi, Kihoon Son, Jaesang Yu, HyunJoon Jung, and Juho Kim (PDF p. 1).

The file is arXiv:2507.22163v4 [cs.HC], stamped 10 May 2026, with the DIS '26 header and DOI 10.1145/3800645.3813005; it has 22 PDF pages. The form identifies this version accurately; no later publisher version was checked (PDF p. 1 and document page count).

The complete markdown conversion was read through its final appendix; appendices A-D are present. Every numerical result retained or added in this check was checked in extracted PDF-page text (PDF pp. 1-22; numerical results especially pp. 9-13 and Tables 1, 2 and 4).

The comparative study includes 12 people, with the same people using both systems; the arm counts of 12 must not be added into 24 distinct participants. No exclusions or randomized headcount are reported, so n_randomized=null is appropriate (PDF pp. 9-10, Sections 6-6.1.2; p. 20, Table 4, P1-P12).

The quoted comparative-study demographics match the source: 5 females, age M=25 and SD=1.71; six graduate design students, three final-year undergraduates, two working design-degree holders, and one graphic designer without a formal degree (PDF pp. 9-10, Section 6.1.1; p. 20, Table 4).

Each person completed two exploration rounds, with a 10-minute tutorial and a 20-minute task per round; the session lasted about 1.5 hours. The stated book-cover and mascot tasks match the source (PDF p. 10, Sections 6.1.1-6.1.2).

The comparison is between generative-AI configurations: DALL-E 3 under both interfaces, ChatGPT available to baseline users, and project-level reuse disabled in the comparative IdeaBlocks condition. GPT-4o supplies the described IdeaBlocks pipeline (PDF pp. 9-10, Sections 4.2.1 and 6.1.3; p. 18, Appendix B.1).

S1-O1 reported string is numerically correct: IdeaBlocks M=0.6384, SD=0.0505; Baseline M=0.5675, SD=0.0897; p=0.0457, with one significance star in Table 1; t=-2.2529 is printed in the text (PDF p. 11, Table 1; p. 12, Section 6.2.3, Flexibility of the Results).

S1-O2 reported string is numerically correct: IdeaBlocks M=123.42, SD=41.66; Baseline M=58 in the table and 58.00 in the text, SD=13.27; p=0.0005, with three significance stars in Table 1 (PDF p. 11, Table 1 and Section 6.2.3, Ideational Fluency).

S1-O3 reported string is numerically correct: IdeaBlocks M=23.25, SD=7.97; Baseline M=13.17, SD=2.66; p=0.0010, with two significance stars in Table 1; t=-4.41 is printed in the text (PDF pp. 10-11, Section 6.2.1; p. 11, Table 1).

The one-line finding accurately reports the comparative sample and both image-count and maximum-distance results. It describes within-session exploration rather than claiming an independently rated overall-creativity benefit (PDF pp. 9-12, Sections 6-6.2.3 and Table 1).

The CLIP measure is the maximum pairwise distance among images generated within each individual session. Coding it as flexibility with question=with_ai is consistent with the codebook; it does not compare outputs across different people (PDF p. 12, Section 6.2.3; creativity-codebook.md Section 6).

Core exclusion and the failed 50-person criterion are supported by the 12-person comparative sample. Keep criterion_1_random_assignment_of_ai='unclear' and context_class='none': no randomized people study is established, there is no AI-versus-human-output comparison or synthesis, and the other studies do not report an eligible observational creativity/diversity contrast (PDF pp. 4, 9-14; creativity-codebook.md Sections 3-4).

The paper is not a synthesis, so the null study/effect-size counts and empty pooled-estimate list are appropriate. Creativity satisfaction and CSI measures are self-reports rather than independent output ratings (PDF pp. 9-14, evaluation studies; p. 12, Perceived Creativity; p. 22, Table 5).
summary: All reported statistics and the 12-person count match the PDF; the study remains below the 50-person threshold. Random assignment is not stated, and the form needs corrections to its design label and incomplete study, overlap, supplement, affiliation, and outcome records.
